sentences.text: Herugavialis is a monotypic genus, containing only the species Herugavialis cairensis that was discovered near Cairo in Egypt.
Unlike all living crocodilians, Herugavialis lacks a maxilla process within its lacrimal gland, a small bony projection normally associated with the eye socket.
The species was reassigned to the newly erected genus Herugavialis in a study published in 2026.
CT imaging shows many anatomical differences between Herugavialis and other Egyptian crocodyliforms such as Eogavialis africanum and Paratomistoma courti.
The species is diagnosed by features including telescoped orbits, meaning the eye sockets are positioned unusually close together.
Herugavialis is placed within Gavialoidea, the superfamily that includes modern gharials and their extinct relatives.
The fossil originates from the Mokattam Formation in Egypt.
Its age is recorded as Middle Miocene in some tables, but other sources assign it to the Eocene Lutetian stage.
One hypothesis argues that the decline of Mediterranean gavialoid diversity resulted from habitat loss linked to global cooling and falling sea levels.
Another view suggests that Miocene warming sparked a temporary resurgence in diversity, which was later ended by the Late Miocene Messinian Salinity Crisis.
